A1.justification: Both PDFs describe VisionTS and provide readable main text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices. The reorganized material can be matched reliably, including the retained experiments and forecasting examples.

before.justification: v3 reports original zero-shot and fine-tuned forecasting results, runtime measurements, ablations, and qualitative examples in the main text and appendices.

after.justification: v4 retains these original empirical results and adds concurrent-baseline comparisons, including an explicitly reported TTM replication.

M1.justification: The period segmentation, normalization, grayscale rendering, bilinear alignment, MAE reconstruction, and inverse forecasting procedure are unchanged. The optional layer-normalization-only fine-tuning strategy is also retained.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same ImageNet pretraining source, eight long-term forecasting datasets, 29 Monash datasets, and 23 GIFT-Eval datasets. The new comparisons reuse six existing long-term datasets.

E2.justification: v4 Appendix B.5 substantially extends direct comparisons with contemporary competitors: Table 13 adds Time-MoE base/large and TTM v1 to long-term zero-shot comparisons, while Table 14 compares CALF against zero-shot and full-shot VisionTS. TTM already appeared in v3's GIFT-Eval comparison, but not in this long-term comparison.

E3.justification: The added comparisons specify Time-MoE base/large and TTM v1 configurations, with Time-MoE's Electricity scores omitted under a data-leakage label. These are limited settings for new comparisons; existing forecast horizons, metrics, validation tuning, and fine-tuning budgets remain unchanged.

E4.justification: The periodicity, backbone, interpolation, orientation, hyperparameter, modality, and fine-tuning analyses are retained, as are the successful and unsuccessful forecasting examples. The new concurrent-baseline tables are ordinary performance comparisons, not new ablations or robustness tests.

E5.justification: Both versions report three-run full-shot experiments and the same standard deviations in v3 Table 18 and v4 Table 20. Runtime measurements remain averaged over 90 runs. The new comparison tables introduce no additional uncertainty-reporting procedure.

E6.justification: v4 Tables 13–14 substantially extend comparative results across the six long-term datasets. Table 13 reports TTM v1 average MSE/MAE of 0.335/0.367 against VisionTS's retained 0.309/0.345, while TTM performs better on Electricity and Weather. Table 14 adds CALF averages of 0.314/0.343 alongside VisionTS's zero-shot and full-shot results. Previously reported scores remain unchanged.

T1.justification: The forecasting definitions and segmentation, normalization, and patch-alignment mathematics are unchanged. Neither version contains additional formal theorems or proofs absent from the other.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list, and conclusion retain the claims that image-pretrained MAE enables competitive zero-shot forecasting and strong performance with minimal fine-tuning. The additional comparisons support the existing contribution without redefining its scientific scope.

C2.justification: v4 qualifies the GIFT-Eval ranking with a historical cutoff and acknowledges stronger subsequent models. Section 4.1 newly suggests possible leakage in those models while asserting that ImageNet pretraining avoids it; the PDFs provide no supporting audit of competitors. Existing mechanism explanations and method limitations are retained.

D1.justification: v4 Table 13 newly identifies the official HuggingFace model as the source for TTM replication and explains that Time-MoE ultra weights were unavailable. VisionTS's code-access statement, software environment, GPU, optimizer, and hyperparameter documentation remain unchanged.

R1.justification: v4 adds citations to Chronos, TTM, Time-MoE, CALF, CBraMod, and HuBERT, with brief discussion of concurrent competitors and masked modeling across fields. The natural-image transfer positioning is retained. The expanded main-text LLM survey already existed in v3 Appendix A.

P1.justification: The text-based related-work survey moves from v3 Appendix A into Section 5, and the remaining appendices are relabeled. v4 adds a concurrent-work subsection, separates the GIFT-Eval and Monash discussion, and updates correspondence, acknowledgments, and publication information. Most prose is retained.

P2.justification: Figure 1 gains a horizontal GIFT-Eval panel redisplaying the existing comparison, and Figure 4 gains a cutoff qualification. Two comparison tables are added, with local rearrangement of figures and appendix tables. The remaining figures and existing table structures are largely retained.

improvement.justification: The added contemporary-baseline comparisons strengthen the assessment of competitiveness, and the explicit GIFT-Eval cutoff improves transparency. These provide a modest net gain within an already extensive evaluation. The new speculation about stronger competitors' data leakage is unsupported within the PDFs and weakens that discussion.
